A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RxnCaption work. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, references, and Appendices A–D support comparison. Internal numerical inconsistencies do not prevent identifying the revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original molecular-detection, reaction-parsing, pilot VQA, and ablation results in Tables 1–6 and Appendices B and D.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments, revises reaction-parsing and ablation results, and adds measured BROS/BIVP inference times in Section 4.3.2.

M1.justification: Both versions retain the YOLOv10-based MolYOLO detector, bounding-box/index visual prompts, Qwen2.5-VL-7B captioner, and JSON reaction extraction. The training-data revisions do not introduce a new model component or parsing procedure.

E1.justification: The documented coverage remains molecular detection, chemical reaction-diagram parsing, and pilot VQA using the same data sources and four reaction-layout categories. RxnCaption-11k becomes RxnCaption-15k, but the reported expansion and augmentation concern sample composition rather than a new domain or task.

E2.justification: The main comparison and detector comparator sets are retained. However, v1's layout comparisons in Appendix D, Figures 7–8, include RxnIM, which v2 omits from the corresponding Figure 8. RxnScribe w/11k and w/15k represent the same retraining baseline under revised data.

E3.justification: Section 3.3 revises the reported training total from 17,442 to 23,432 images, changes RxnScribe sampling, and adds targeted augmentation of reversible and unusual-direction reactions. Section 4.1.3 changes HybridMatch: BROS gains text-content fallback, while BIVP requires exact reactant/product text matches. These substantially revise training and evaluation settings, although v2's Table 3 conflicts with its new training-data count.

E4.justification: v2 adds a latency analysis testing whether the two-stage design increases computational overhead. Existing detector-substitution, ideal-stage error attribution, and layout analyses remain, with revised results and a narrower F1-only layout breakdown. Layout analysis already appeared in v1 Appendix D; its new main-text placement is not a new experiment.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The parenthesized red values added to v2 Table 6 are performance differences, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Table 4 substantially revises trained-model results. RxnCaption-VL BIVP Hybrid/Soft F1 changes from 75.5/88.2 to 72.2/86.2 on RxnScribe and from 55.5/67.6 to 59.8/70.4 on the authors' benchmark. Changed training and matching rules prevent treating these as controlled performance gains or losses. Appendix ablation and layout results also change; layout precision/recall entries disappear, and new latency results report 16.88 seconds/image for BROS versus 9.65 for BIVP.

T1.justification: Section 4.1.3 revises HybridMatch's mathematical acceptance rule: BROS text can match through IoU or content, and BIVP reactant/product text requires exact matching instead of the previous normalized-edit-distance tolerance. The set-based reaction-task definition remains unchanged, and neither version supplies theoretical proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: visual-prompt reaction parsing, a large real-literature dataset, state-of-the-art molecular detection, and leading RxnCaption-VL performance. Updating the dataset designation from 11k to 15k does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the explanation of retrained RxnScribe's decline with discussion of gains on both benchmarks and stronger dataset-generalization interpretations. It adds shorter-output reasoning for the latency advantage and structural-robustness interpretations of layout results. The reaction-extraction bottleneck and Section 6 limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 specifies retaining non-overlapping MolYOLO predictions with IoU below 0.5 in the ideal-detector analysis, documents targeted augmentation, and identifies a single 80GB A100 for latency measurement. The dataset access reference changes to RxnCaption-15k. Existing optimizer, training-hardware, schedule, and appendix prompt details are largely retained.

R1.justification: The same 48 references and Appendix A related-work discussion are retained. Positioning against coordinate-prediction approaches and synthetic reaction data remains substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 locally rewrites metric, results, and ablation explanations, reverses the two original ablation subsections, adds a main-text layout subsection, and expands Appendix D discussion. Dataset terminology and author information also change. Most of the document's narrative and section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: The layout-result presentation is substantially rebuilt: v1's separate precision/recall/F1 Figures 7–8 become a combined F1-only Figure 8 organized by model, with a separate main-text view in Figure 5. The error-attribution table gains reordered metrics and highlighted differences. Figures 1–4 also receive graphical, sizing, or legend revisions.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful latency evidence and clearer matching/control descriptions, but introduces reporting conflicts: Table 3 retains 10,112 training images while Section 3.3 states 15,128, and Table 5 retains RxnCaption-VL's RxnScribe Hybrid F1 of 75.5 while Tables 4 and 18 report 72.2. These new inconsistencies weaken confidence in the empirical revision. The documentation gains and reporting harms leave the net effect on overall quality unclear.
